prompt: People are now living much longer lives than before and many feel we should remain in the workforce for longer. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Although some people believe that individuals should remain in the workforce for longer because life expectancy has increased compared with the past, I strongly disagree with this view. In my opinion, delaying retirement can reduce employment opportunities for younger people and prevent workplaces from benefiting from fresh ideas and perspectives.

To begin with, requiring people to work until an older age could reduce job opportunities for younger generations. Many experienced employees occupy senior positions for a longer period when they delay retirement, which can make it more difficult for younger workers to enter the workforce or receive promotions. As a result, young people may struggle to gain valuable experience and develop their careers. For example, if senior employees remain in the same positions for several additional years, newly qualified graduates may have fewer opportunities to obtain permanent jobs in their chosen fields. Therefore, maintaining a reasonable retirement age can help create a better balance between different generations in the workplace.

Another important reason is that younger workers can bring fresh ideas, modern skills and new perspectives to organisations. Although older employees have valuable experience and knowledge, workplaces also need people who are familiar with recent technologies and changing trends. Younger employees are often more comfortable with new digital tools and may introduce innovative ways of completing tasks. For instance, a company that hires recent graduates may benefit from their knowledge of artificial intelligence, social media and other modern technologies. Consequently, replacing some retiring employees with younger workers can help organisations remain competitive and adaptable.

However, this does not mean that older employees should be forced to retire completely. Those who are healthy and willing to continue working should have the option of taking part-time positions, consulting roles or flexible jobs. In this way, they can share their valuable experience with younger employees while gradually reducing their workload.

In conclusion, I strongly disagree that people should generally be expected to remain in the workforce for longer simply because they are living longer. A reasonable retirement age is important because it provides opportunities for younger workers while allowing organisations to benefit from new ideas and modern skills. Nevertheless, older people who wish to continue working should be given flexible options.
